name: Tessy Thomas
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; joined DRDO as a junior scientist in 1988 at age 25, but her first major achievement (Agni Self Reliance Award) came in 2001 at age 38.
early_history_summary: Thomas grew up near a rocket launching station in Kerala and developed an early fascination with rockets. She earned a B.Tech in electrical engineering and an M.Tech in guided missiles, joining DRDO's missile lab in 1988 as a junior scientist.
family_context_summary: Born to a small-businessman father and homemaker mother in Alappuzha, Kerala; father suffered a stroke when she was young, leaving the family in modest circumstances.
evidence_summary: Thomas joined DRDO in 1988 at age 25 as a junior scientist working on guidance systems, but her first independently verifiable milestone (Agni Self Reliance Award) did not occur until 2001 at age 38. She became Project Director of Agni-IV in 2009 at age 46. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

early_history_summary: Born in Romania to Transylvanian Saxon parents, Holmes's family sought political asylum in Germany in 1968. He dropped out of school, worked in fashion and IT sales, and did not begin his adult film career until age 35.
family_context_summary: Born to Transylvanian Saxon parents in Sibiu, Romania; family emigrated to Germany seeking political asylum in 1968.
evidence_summary: Holmes spent his twenties and early thirties working in fashion, IT sales, and other jobs. He performed his first pornographic scene in November 1996 at age 35. His first award (NINFA for Best Supporting Actor) came in 2001 at age 40. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Claes-Ingvar Lagerkvist
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Lagerkvist earned his PhD in 1977 at age 33 and his asteroid/comet discoveries came in the 1990s.
early_history_summary: Lagerkvist studied at Uppsala University and became an astronomer at the Uppsala Astronomical Observatory. His PhD was awarded in 1977, and his notable discoveries of comets and asteroids occurred in the 1990s.
evidence_summary: Lagerkvist's PhD was awarded in 1977 at age 33, and his comet and asteroid discoveries occurred in 1996 at age 52. No specific, dated, material milestone by age 26 (circa 1970) was found in reviewed sources.

name: Stig Blomqvist
milestone_by_age_26: Won three international rallies in 1971 (Swedish Rally, 1000 Lakes Rally, RAC Rally) with Saab, scoring 11 wins in 16 rallies that year.
early_history_summary: Blomqvist grew up in a rallying family in Örebro, Sweden; his father competed locally and his uncle owned a car garage where Stig learned car control on frozen lakes from age 10. He acquired his driving licence at 18 and immediately took second place in a 1964 local rally, then joined the Saab factory team.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Örebro, Sweden; father was a local-level rally competitor and uncle owned a car garage, providing early access to vehicles and driving practice.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father rally competitor, uncle car garage, early driving age 10, frozen lake practice, Saab factory support
evidence_summary: Blomqvist's father and uncle were directly involved in motorsport and car ownership, giving him access to driving from age 10 on frozen lakes. He co-drove for his father at 12 and began serious rallying at 18 in 1964, quickly attracting Saab factory support by 1965. By 1971 at age 24-25, he won three major international rallies and scored 11 wins in 16 events, establishing himself as one of the world's top rally drivers. His early immersion in Swedish winter rallying was a direct product of his family domain.
starting_point: Born in Örebro, Sweden to a family immersed in local motorsport; father was a local rally competitor and uncle owned a car garage.
current_position: Retired Swedish rally driver; 1984 World Rally Champion; lives in Saffron Walden, Essex, UK; son Tom Blomqvist is a professional racing driver.

trajectory.event: Acquired driving licence and immediately took second place in a local rally near Karlstad with a Saab 96.

name: Rakhat Aliyev
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Aliyev was a clinical resident and postgraduate at a surgical institute through 1989, with his rise to power beginning only after Kazakhstan's independence in 1991.
early_history_summary: Born in Alma-Ata, Kazakh SSR, Aliyev married Dariga Nazarbayeva (daughter of future president Nursultan Nazarbayev) in 1983. He worked as a surgeon and researcher at the Kazakh Research Institute of Surgery from 1986 to 1993 before entering politics and business after independence.
family_context_summary: Born in Alma-Ata to a family from the Qonyrat clan; married Dariga Nazarbayeva in 1983, daughter of Nursultan Nazarbayev who became Kazakhstan's president.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; his political and business career was built through his marriage into the Nazarbayev family.
evidence_summary: Aliyev's career was built on his 1983 marriage into the Nazarbayev family, but his material rise to power (tax police chief, KNB deputy chief, ambassador) occurred in the late 1990s and 2000s, well after age 26. From 1986 to 1993 he was a clinical resident and researcher at a surgical institute. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Kevin Keegan
milestone_by_age_26: Won the First Division title and UEFA Cup with Liverpool in the 1972-73 season at age 22, establishing himself as one of England's top forwards.
early_history_summary: Born to a coal-mining family in Armthorpe, Yorkshire, Keegan was rejected by Coventry and Doncaster for being too small. He played Sunday league football, was signed by Scunthorpe United as an apprentice at 15, and made his debut at 17. Bill Shankly signed him for Liverpool in May 1971 for £35,000, where he formed a devastating strike partnership with John Toshack.
family_context_summary: Born to a coal-mining family in Armthorpe, Yorkshire; father Joe was a miner and Newcastle United supporter who had served in Burma during WWII. Working-class background with no football connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Liverpool FC under Shankly, Toshack strike partnership, overcame size rejection, working-class background
evidence_summary: Keegan came from a working-class mining family with no football connections and was rejected by professional clubs for being too small. He built himself up through relentless Sunday league football and weight training, earning a Scunthorpe apprenticeship at 15. Bill Shankly signed him for Liverpool at 20 and personally molded him into a star, forming a devastating partnership with John Toshack. By 22, Keegan had won the First Division and UEFA Cup, and by 26 he had added the European Cup. His trajectory was driven by elite coaching at Liverpool and sheer determination.
starting_point: Born to a coal-mining family in Armthorpe, Yorkshire; father was a colliery worker and WWII veteran who had moved from Durham to find work in the pits.
current_position: Died on 20 July 2026 at age 75 after battling stage four cancer; final role: former England player and manager, Liverpool and Newcastle legend, twice Ballon d'Or winner (1978, 1979).

trajectory.event: Made professional debut for Scunthorpe United in the Fourth Division.
Signed for Liverpool for £35,000 by Bill Shankly and scored on his debut against Nottingham Forest.
Won the First Division title and UEFA Cup with Liverpool, scoring 22 goals in all competitions.

Retired from professional playing after helping Newcastle United secure promotion to the First Division.
Died on 20 July 2026 after battling stage four cancer.

name: Vince McMahon
milestone_by_age_26: No material independent milestone by age 26; McMahon worked as a ring announcer and commentator for his father's wrestling promotion in the early 1970s, with his transformative achievement (buying and nationalizing the company) occurring in 1982 at age 37.
early_history_summary: McMahon met his father, wrestling promoter Vincent J. McMahon, at age 12 and became determined to enter the business. He graduated from East Carolina University in 1968 and began working for his father's WWWF as a ring announcer and commentator in the early 1970s, assigned to the small Bangor, Maine territory.
family_context_summary: Born in Pinehurst, North Carolina; parents divorced when he was very young and he grew up in a trailer with his mother and successive stepfathers. Met his birth father, wrestling promoter Vincent J. McMahon, at age 12.
evidence_summary: McMahon's early wrestling work (1969-1971) consisted of being a commentator and ring announcer for his father's promotion, which is a family-assigned job rather than an independent material milestone. His transformative achievements — buying the company in 1982, creating WrestleMania, and nationalizing wrestling — all occurred after age 37. No material independent milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Mike Burton
milestone_by_age_26: Won two Olympic gold medals at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics in the 400m and 1500m freestyle at age 21.
early_history_summary: Burton was hit by a furniture truck while bicycling at age 13, ending his contact-sport aspirations and leaving swimming as his only fitness option. He joined the Arden Hills Swim Club under Hall of Fame coach Sherm Chavoor in Sacramento, won 10 AAU titles in high school, and swam at UCLA under coach Bob Horn, becoming a pioneer of mega-mileage training.
family_context_summary: Son of a truck driver; family moved from Des Moines, Iowa to Sacramento, California. Working-class background with no swimming connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: truck accident age 13, Arden Hills Swim Club, Sherm Chavoor coaching, mega-mileage training pioneer, UCLA
evidence_summary: Burton's swimming career was born from adversity: a truck accident at 13 left him unable to play contact sports, channeling him into swimming under Hall of Fame coach Sherm Chavoor at Arden Hills Swim Club. Chavoor's revolutionary over-distance training approach matched Burton's extraordinary work ethic, earning him the nickname 'Mr. Machine.' By 20 he won Pan Am Games gold, and at 21 he won two Olympic golds at Mexico City. His trajectory was defined by the constraint of injury, elite coaching, and unprecedented training intensity.
starting_point: Son of a truck driver; born in Des Moines, Iowa, family moved to Sacramento, California where he grew up in North Highlands.
current_position: Retired swimmer and swimming coach; three-time Olympic gold medalist; inducted into International Swimming Hall of Fame in 1977; lives in the United States.

trajectory.event: Competed at the US Olympic Trials in the 1500m freestyle, finishing fifth and narrowly missing the Olympic team.
Won gold in the 1500m freestyle at the Pan American Games and gold at the University Games in Tokyo.
Won two Olympic gold medals at Mexico City in the 400m and 1500m freestyle despite being ill during the competition.
Won Olympic gold in the 1500m freestyle at Munich in world record time, becoming the first man to win two Olympic 1500m titles.
Inducted into the International Swimming Hall of Fame as an Honor Swimmer.

name: John Hurt
milestone_by_age_26: Cast as Richard Rich in the film A Man for All Seasons (released December 1966), which won the Academy Award for Best Picture; this was his first major film role and brought him to prominence.
early_history_summary: Born to an Anglican clergyman father and an engineer/former-actress mother in Derbyshire, Hurt developed a passion for acting at his prep school in Kent. After art school, he won a scholarship to RADA in 1960, made his professional stage and film debut in 1962, and attracted director Fred Zinnemann's attention through his stage performance in Little Malcolm, leading to his casting in A Man for All Seasons.
family_context_summary: Born to an Anglican clergyman (former mathematician) father and an engineer and one-time actress mother in Chesterfield, Derbyshire; middle-class family with a strict upbringing. Sent to prep school at age 8.
primary_early_advantage_tags: RADA scholarship, London theatre, prep school acting, Zinnemann casting, middle-class education
evidence_summary: Hurt benefited from a middle-class upbringing that provided access to prep school theatre and an RADA scholarship, the key institutional pipeline for British acting. His mother's brief acting career provided some domain proximity. His stage work in Little Malcolm attracted Fred Zinnemann, who cast him in A Man for All Seasons at 26. Despite a strict upbringing and parental opposition to acting, the institutional ecosystem of RADA and London theatre accelerated his early career.
starting_point: Born in Chesterfield, Derbyshire to an Anglican clergyman father (formerly a mathematician) and a mother who was an engineer and one-time actress; middle-class family with a strict religious upbringing.
current_position: Died on 25 January 2017 at age 77; final roles included roles in films such as Jackie and Darkest Hour; knighted in 2015 for services to drama.

trajectory.event: Made professional film debut in The Wild and the Willing and began performing on the London stage after graduating from RADA.
Cast as Richard Rich in A Man for All Seasons, his first major film role; the film won the Academy Award for Best Picture.
Won the BAFTA for Best Actor for his portrayal of Quentin Crisp in The Naked Civil Servant.
Earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor for Midnight Express.
Earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor for The Elephant Man.
Knighted by Queen Elizabeth II for services to drama.
Died on 25 January 2017 in Norfolk, England.

name: Jean-Pierre Beltoise
milestone_by_age_26: Won 11 French national motorcycle road racing titles between 1961 and 1963, establishing himself as one of France's top motorcycle racers by age 24-26.
early_history_summary: Born into a working-class Parisian family where his father owned a butcher shop, Beltoise developed a passion for mechanical machines and started riding motorcycles in 1955 at age 18. He won 11 French national championships in three years and competed in international Grand Prix motorcycle racing before a near-fatal crash in 1964 forced his switch to car racing.
family_context_summary: Born into a working-class Parisian family in Boulogne-Billancourt; father owned a butcher shop and Beltoise made deliveries as a youth.
primary_early_advantage_tags: 11 French national motorcycle titles, working-class background, self-taught motorcycle racing, mechanical passion
evidence_summary: Beltoise came from a working-class family with no motorsport connections; his father was a butcher. He taught himself motorcycle racing from age 18 and won an extraordinary 11 French national titles in three years through sheer talent and repetition. No family financial support, mentor, or elite pipeline was documented for his early motorcycle career. His later switch to F1 car racing was catalyzed by a near-fatal crash in 1964 that permanently damaged his arm, making his subsequent F1 career all the more remarkable.
starting_point: Born into a working-class Parisian family in Boulogne-Billancourt; father owned a butcher shop where Beltoise worked making deliveries.
current_position: Died on 5 January 2015 at age 77 in Dakar, Senegal; final career: French racing driver who won the 1972 Monaco Grand Prix with BRM, his only Formula 1 victory.

name: Álvaro Siza Vieira
milestone_by_age_26: Completed his first built works (four houses in Matosinhos) and opened his private architecture practice in Porto in 1954 at age 21, before even graduating.
early_history_summary: Siza grew up in a bourgeois Roman Catholic family in Matosinhos, near Porto. His father commissioned him to design a garden pavilion at age 13-14, his first built project. He enrolled in the architecture program at the Porto Fine Arts School in 1949 at age 16, and by 1954 had completed four houses and opened his own practice, later collaborating with his teacher Fernando Távora.
family_context_summary: Grew up in a large Roman Catholic bourgeois family in Matosinhos, near Porto; father Júlio Siza Vieira owned a family home and commissioned Álvaro's first architectural project at age 13-14.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father as first client, bourgeois family, Porto School of Architecture, Fernando Távora mentor, early built works
evidence_summary: Siza's father played a direct role in his early architectural development by commissioning a garden pavilion when Álvaro was only 13-14, providing his first real design-build experience. The bourgeois family background enabled education at the Porto Fine Arts School from age 16. His collaboration with teacher and colleague Fernando Távora from 1955-58 further accelerated his development. By 21, he had four built houses and his own practice — an unusually early start for an architect, driven by family support and domain exposure.
starting_point: Born in Matosinhos, Portugal to a bourgeois Roman Catholic family; father Júlio Siza Vieira owned a family home and commissioned Álvaro's first architectural project at age 13-14.
current_position: Portuguese architect, still active at age 92; Pritzker Prize laureate (1992); maintains a practice in Porto, Portugal.

trajectory.event: Completed his first built works (four houses in Matosinhos) and opened his private architecture practice in Porto, before graduating.

name: Björn Waldegård
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Swedish Rally Championship in 1967 at age 24 with a Porsche 911, establishing himself as a national champion and top-level rally driver.
early_history_summary: Born in Rimbo, Sweden, Waldegård's father competed in rallying at a low level and took seven-year-old Björn to watch local Swedish rallies. He bought his first Volkswagen Beetle in 1962 at age 19 and began competing, showing immediate talent with a podium on the Swedish Rally within three years. He switched to a Porsche 911 in 1967 and won the Swedish Rally Championship two years running.
family_context_summary: Born in Rimbo, Sweden; father competed in rallying at a low level and took young Björn to watch local rallies from age 7-8, igniting his passion for the sport.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father rally competitor, early rally exposure age 7-8, Swedish rally ecosystem, Porsche factory support, natural talent
evidence_summary: Waldegård's father was a local rally competitor who took him to watch rallies from age 7-8, providing direct early domain immersion. He began competing at 19 with a VW Beetle and showed immediate natural talent, reaching the Swedish Rally podium within three years. By 24, he won the Swedish Rally Championship with a Porsche 911 supplied by the Swedish importer, and at 25 he won the Monte Carlo Rally as a Porsche factory driver. His trajectory was driven by family domain exposure, natural driving talent, and the Swedish rally ecosystem.
starting_point: Born in Rimbo, Sweden to a family with local rallying connections; father competed in rallying at a low level and took young Björn to watch local rallies from age 7-8.
current_position: Died on 29 August 2014 at age 70 in Stockholm, Sweden; final career: first World Rally Champion (1979), 16 WRC victories, drove for Porsche, Lancia, Ford, Toyota, and Mercedes-Benz.

trajectory.event: Made his rally debut with a Volkswagen Beetle in Swedish national events.
